chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
The tongue of the wise man is behind his heart, and the heart of the fool is behind his tongue.

key_terms.الْأَحْمَقِ: The fool, one lacking in wisdom or discernment
key_terms.الْعَاقِلِ: The wise person, one who possesses intellect and discernment
key_terms.قَلْبُ: The heart, representing the seat of thought, intention, and contemplation
key_terms.لِسَانُ: The tongue, representing speech or expression

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the speech of a wise person and a foolish person according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This maxim highlights the epistemological hierarchy in Shia ethics, where the heart (qalb) serves as the seat of insight (basirah) and the tongue as its instrument. Sharif al-Radi’s compilation emphasizes that true wisdom requires the intellect to govern speech, whereas folly is characterized by the loss of internal control, allowing unrefined thoughts to dictate external expression.
